# Summary

This ARFC proposes onboarding PT-AUSD-8OCT2026, the PT for Agora's AUSD to the [PROJECT] V3 instance on Monad.

# Motivation

## Overview

[PROJECT] went live on Monad in [MONTH] [YEAR] and crossed 300M USD in deposits, with AUSD onboarded as one of the instance's core stablecoin reserves. AUSD is Agora's institutional digital dollar, minted 1:1 against USD and backed by cash, short-dated U.S. Treasury bills and overnight reverse repurchase agreements. The reserve fund is managed by VanEck, with State Street acting as cash custodian and fund administrator, and reserves are independently attested by Grant Thornton. AUSD is currently the largest stablecoin on Monad, and Pendle operates a liquid AUSD market on the chain.

## Rationale for Onboarding PT-AUSD-8OCT2026

Onboarding this maturity would enable users to use their fixed-yield PT-AUSD positions as collateral within the same [PROJECT] market that already supports AUSD, further enhancing the utility and capital efficiency of the stablecoin on [PROJECT]'s latest deployment.

As a short-dated, AUSD-backed asset, PT-AUSD offers a collateral profile that is well aligned with [PROJECT]'s risk framework, making it a strong candidate for inclusion on Monad.

Selected market data at the time of submission:

| Metric | Value |
|----|----|
| Underlying asset | AUSD (Agora) |
| Maturity | [DATE] |
| Residual maturity at submission | Approximately 85 days |
| PT implied APY | Approximately 6.5% |
| Pendle market liquidity | Approximately 5.75M USD |
| PT total value locked | Approximately 67.5M USD |
| 7-day trading volume | Approximately 8.06M USD |

The case for onboarding rests on the following points:

1. Incentives from Agora. Agora has committed some incentives towards that Pendle market we can see the current implied rate around 6.5% APR being subsidized with incentives.
2. Underlying already onboarded. AUSD is already a live reserve on the [PROJECT] Monad instance, so the market already prices AUSD and the collateral pairing is natural: PT-AUSD supplied as collateral against AUSD or other stablecoin debt within a dedicated E-Mode category.
3. Ecosystem growth. Enabling PT-AUSD as collateral supports stablecoin leverage and borrowing demand on a nascent instance, aligned with the growth objectives set out in the [PROJECT] Protocol v3.7 Monad deployment.

## Oracle

**Price Feed Recommendation**

For pricing PT-AUSD-8OCT2026 on [PROJECT], the dynamic linear discount rate oracle is recommended. The same oracle template currently in use for Pendle PT assets on [PROJECT] V3, can be reused for this deployment.

The oracle prices the PT as a zero-coupon bond against a capped underlying Chainlink reference (AUSD/USD fixed at 1 USD), applying a linear discount that decays to par at maturity. The discount rate is bounded above by the maxDiscountRatePerYear parameter, providing a deterministic price floor against adverse market dislocations.

**Discount Rate Parameters**

| Parameter | PT-AUSD-8OCT2026 |
|----|----|
| initialDiscountRatePerYear | To be provided by Risk Service Providers |
| maxDiscountRatePerYear | To be provided by Risk Service Providers |

Given the current on-chain liquidity of the PT-AUSD market on Monad (approximately 5.75M USD), a conservative initial supply cap and a collateral configuration consistent with the treatment of comparable short-dated Pendle PT stablecoin assets on other [PROJECT] instances is anticipated.

# SAEP-19: Remove the [PROJECT] Risk Council - [DATE]

[PROJECT]'s Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review
The [PROJECT] community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes, as described by the author of the proposal:

> ## Proposal Details
> 
> We propose that [PROJECT] governance remove the [PROJECT] Risk Council from the [PROJECT] Artifact and reassign its functions as follows:
> 
> - Remove the mandatory SRC review step from the Root Edit Routine Protocol. The Operational Facilitator review step remains in place unchanged as the pre-vote gate for alignment, author eligibility, and operational feasibility.
> - Remove the “Passed SRC Review” precondition from the Root Edit Token Holder Vote, so that the Operational Facilitator triggers the Snapshot poll upon a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and [PROJECT] Artifact.
> - Transfer responsibility for immediate Delegate offboarding to the [PROJECT] Foundation, which already manages Delegate onboarding, identity verification, sanctions checks, and term re-approvals ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.1]([URL] [A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.3]([URL] and requests the KYC whose failure is a ground for emergency removal. The existing registry-update process on offboarding ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.5.4]([URL] is unchanged.
> - Transfer initiation of a Delegate Removal vote on disqualification grounds to the [PROJECT] Foundation, consistent with the reassignment of emergency offboarding and with the [PROJECT] Foundation’s existing role in collecting the information on which the disqualification grounds turn.
> - Transfer the Delegate compromised-key response to the [PROJECT] Foundation, which maintains the Registry of Delegates in which a compromised Delegate is flagged and through which a replacement verified address is processed.
> - Amend the Risk Curation Framework cancellation reasons so that risk-based cancellation of pending changes continues to rely on identification by the Sky Core Council. The cancellation authorities ([PROJECT] SubDAO Proxy and Guardian) and all timelock controls are unchanged.
> - Amend the Private Ecosystem Review provision so that confidential pre-activation disclosure is made to the applicable Sky ecosystem governance reviewers designated for confidential ecosystem reviews. The objection right, the bar on activation while an objection is unresolved, and the orderly wind-down requirement are unchanged.
> - Remove the [PROJECT] Risk Council section of the [PROJECT] Artifact ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4]([URL] and all subdocuments, including the SRC membership registry.
> 
> If approved, any Root Edit proposal pending SRC review at the time the Artifact update takes effect proceeds under the amended Routine Protocol. Any Delegate suspension in effect under [A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.7.2]([URL] at the time the Artifact update takes effect continues in effect and is administered by the [PROJECT] Foundation. If approved, Phoenix Labs intends to coordinate with the [PROJECT] Foundation and the currently seated SRC members on an orderly wind-down of their engagements in accordance with the existing compensation terms approved by the [PROJECT] Foundation.
> 
> ## Justification
> 
> **Overlapping safeguards remain in place.** Each function performed by the SRC is also performed, or backstopped, by an actor whose mandate exists independently of this proposal, with the single exception identified under “What is not replicated” below. Pre-vote alignment review of every Root Edit proposal is conducted by the Operational Facilitator, who is required to prevent misaligned proposals from proceeding ([A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3]([URL] [A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6]([URL] the [PROJECT] Artifact already directs the Operational Facilitator to advance aligned proposals to Snapshot without an SRC conclusion when the SRC does not act within its review window ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.3.3]([URL] so the consolidated process this proposal adopts is one the Artifact already sanctions. Downstream of any vote, every resulting Artifact update or action passes through the Operational Executor Agent, whose duty to check Prime Agent actions for Atlas alignment cannot be amended by Prime Agents or Executor Agents ([A.1.14.4.4.1]([URL] and who may refuse to operationalize actions that are misaligned or present significant risk beyond its insured capacity ([A.1.14.4.5]([URL] Core GovOps may review the [PROJECT] Artifact for Atlas compliance at any time and directly edit it to enforce conformance ([A.1.[DATE].2.1]([URL] [A.1.[DATE].1.2]([URL] and the Sky Executive Vote may override any Agent Artifact provision on misalignment or safety grounds ([A.1.14.1.6.1]([URL] These Sky Atlas-level safeguards exist independently of the [PROJECT] Artifact and are unaffected by this proposal. In addition to these codified mechanisms, ongoing risk analysis and review of [PROJECT]-related activity is performed by Sky-affiliated actors including the Sky Core Council, risk team contributors at the Sky Frontier Foundation, and the Core Council Risk Advisor(s). This proposal does not alter their mandates, and no [PROJECT] Artifact language change is required for their work to continue.
> 
> **The Root Edit Primitive continues to satisfy its Sky Core specification**. The Sky Atlas requires that the Root Edit Primitive “must specify the requirements for proposals to be included in a vote, such as any required review period or any reviews that must be conducted by other parties such as expert advisors” ([A.2.2.6.2.2.2.3]([URL] That requirement is to specify the applicable requirements, and the examples it gives are illustrative rather than mandatory. After this change, the [PROJECT] Root Edit Routine Protocol continues to specify a seven (7) day Operational Facilitator review with a published alignment finding, the conditions under which a proposal advances, and a three (3) day token holder vote with a stated approval threshold. The Primitive therefore remains fully specified, and removing the document titled “Root Edit Expert Advisor Review” does not leave a gap against A.2.2.6.2.2.2.3.
> 
> **Process efficiency.** The SRC review is a serial step of up to seven (7) days in every Root Edit cycle, and the SRC is a compensated three-member body ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.6]([URL] Removing the step shortens the path from submission to Snapshot for every future Root Edit and eliminates the ongoing compensation cost, without removing the blocking alignment gate (Operational Facilitator) or the non-amendable execution-layer check (Operational Executor Agent).
> **Each reassigned function has a named decision-maker.** After this change, the pre-vote gate for Root Edits is the Operational Facilitator; emergency Delegate removal, initiation of a Delegate Removal vote on disqualification grounds, and the Delegate compromised-key response are decided by the [PROJECT] Foundation, which already conducts the identity verification, conflict-of-interest collection, and sanctions checks on which the removal and disqualification grounds turn ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.1]([URL] and which maintains the Registry of Delegates in which a suspension is recorded; risk identification for Risk Curation cancellations rests with the Sky Core Council, which is already named in the same provision; and confidential pre-activation review of a Confidential Strategic Integration and Deployment rests with the Sky ecosystem governance reviewers designated for confidential ecosystem reviews, who are already named in the same provision and already hold the objection right that gates activation. No function is left with criteria but no decider.
> 
> **What is not replicated.** Two capabilities are narrowed rather than re-housed. The first is a structured, public, pre-vote risk analysis published for every Root Edit proposal, which is unique to the SRC and which this proposal does not re-house. Risk analysis coverage of [PROJECT]-related activity continues through the Sky-affiliated actors noted above, proposals remain open to public review on the Sky Forum throughout the governance cycle, the Operational Facilitator’s review remains a blocking gate, and token holders retain the ability to reject any proposal at Snapshot. The second is the SRC’s seat as a confidential disclosure recipient prior to activation of a Confidential Strategic Integration and Deployment, which narrows that review to the Sky ecosystem governance reviewers designated for confidential ecosystem reviews. The substance of the review is unchanged: disclosure of all relevant deployment details remains mandatory before activation, the reviewers’ objection right is unchanged, and activation remains barred while an objection is unresolved.

Additional details can be found in the [proposal forum post]([URL]

The proposed [PROJECT] Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: [URL]

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into [PROJECT]'s artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.

Titel: Special Council Elections – [MONTH] [YEAR] Cohort

## Abstract

This proposal calls for the **[MONTH] cohort Special Council election** to begin on **[DATE], at 17:00 UTC** and run for **seven (7) days**, ending on **[DATE], at 17:00 UTC**. This election will fill **four (4) Special Council seats**, as designated in the [PROJECT] DAO Constitution.

## Background

The Special Council is a 7-member body tasked with providing oversight, reviewing proposals, and ensuring the security and financial stability of the [PROJECT] DAO. To maintain continuity while allowing for community input, the council operates on a staggered election schedule:

- **[MONTH] Cohort:** 3 seats
- **[MONTH] Cohort:** 4 seats

This proposal ensures the timely execution of the election, allowing tokenholders to select representatives for these four Special Council seats. The newly elected members will officially begin their term in [MONTH].

This is the first Special Council vote under [PROJECT]'s updated Snapshot setup. Voting power counts self-custodied [TOKEN] held on Base, held on [PROJECT] L3, and staked in `base:[ADDRESS]`.

The four seats of the [MONTH] cohort are up for election. Current council members **Lukas Bures**, **Vladan Nikolic**, **Jemma Xu**, and **Paul Mihalache** are running for re-election.

## Election Details

- **Start Date:** [DATE], at 17:00 UTC
- **End Date:** [DATE], at 17:00 UTC
- **Seats Available:** 4 Special Council seats ([MONTH] cohort)
- **Voting Method:** Snapshot
- **Voting System:** Weighted Voting – each voter may spread voting power across any number of choices
- **Winners:** The four candidates with the highest number of votes will be elected to the Special Council

Candidates must meet the eligibility criteria set forth in the [PROJECT] DAO Constitution, including:

- Experience in web3, governance, or community leadership
- Background in community engagement and community safety
- An entrepreneurial mindset and excellent communication skills
- No conflicts of interest (e.g., no more than 2 SC members from the same entity)
- Compliance with nationality requirements (at least 5 SC members must be non-US persons)

Titel: Adopt the CMv2 Penalty Framework

## Summary

This proposal introduces the [Penalty Framework for the Curated Module v2 (CMv2)]([URL] as the baseline process for assessing and applying penalties to Node Operators. The Framework establishes how [the Curated Module Committee (CMC)]([URL] with analysis and support from the NOM team (Node Operator Mechanisms workstream of DAO contributors), reviews incidents involving Node Operator conduct, misconfiguration, underperformance, or other protocol-impacting events.

This framework does not presume automatic penalties. Each incident is assessed on a case-by-case basis against factors such as impact, cause, preventability, responsiveness, transparency, recurrence, and whether the Node Operator took steps to avoid greater protocol risk. 

Approving this Framework also establishes how it can be maintained going forward: the CMC becomes authorised to update operational elements specified below without a separate DAO vote for each change, provided the core principles, penalty mechanisms, Node Operator obligations, and governance structure remain unchanged.

## Background

Node Operators operate validators as part of the [PROJECT] protocol. Failures in validator operations, such as missed block attestations or proposals, insecure key handling, delayed withdrawals, slashing, or misdirected execution layer rewards, can create direct and/or indirect losses for stakers and reputational risk for the [PROJECT] protocol. Not every such failure reflects Node Operator fault: some arise from causes outside their reasonable control, such as client bugs, relay failures, network-wide events, or coordinated risk mitigation. Hence, incidents need to be assessed on their specific circumstances rather than resolved through a fixed rulebook. This Framework sets out the principles, factors, and process that guide that assessment.

Penalties are not intended to be punitive by default. They exist to:

1. Compensate the protocol for identifiable losses, missed rewards, or improperly redirected rewards.
2. Discourage conduct that creates avoidable operational, security, or reputational risk.
3. Encourage timely remediation and cooperation by Node Operators.
4. Protect stakers and the protocol from losses caused by preventable conduct or non-compliance.
5. Preserve the integrity and reliability of the Curated Module v2.

## Core Principles

- **Proportionality**. The penalty amount should be proportionate to the actual or reasonably estimated harm, including direct losses, missed or misdirected rewards, added operational cost, and the risk the incident introduced to the protocol, adjusted for relevant aggravating or mitigating circumstances.
- **Accountability**. Where harm results from conduct the Node Operator could reasonably have prevented, such as misconfiguration, poor key management, inadequate monitoring, inadequate backup or failover arrangements, slow response, or deliberate misconduct, the CMC can apply a penalty and/or recommend additional measures. Harm resulting from causes genuinely outside the Node Operator’s control should be assessed accordingly, and such incidents may be considered as carrying less weight in the assessment of accountability.
- **Preservation of protocol safety**. The Framework shouldn't create an incentive to take unsafe action just to avoid a penalty. If a Node Operator, in coordination with NOM or other relevant [PROJECT] contributors, takes conservative action to reduce slashing or key-compromise risk, even if that results in downtime or missed rewards, that decision should be assessed in light of the risk avoided.
- **Case-by-case assessment and non-exhaustivity**. The CMC assesses each incident on its own facts, treating the Framework's categories as reference points rather than a rulebook of automatic triggers. Matching a listed category doesn't guarantee a penalty, and falling outside one doesn't guarantee immunity: the CMC can act on a pattern, a combination of incidents, or repeated lower-severity issues that don't fit into a single category. A list of common incident categories is provided in the [forum post]([URL] for illustration and is not exhaustive.

## Assessment Factors

Assessment considers two key aspects: the actual event, its **impact**, **duration**, **cause**, **intent**, **preventability** and the way the Node Operator responded, including **responsiveness**, **coordination**, **transparency**, and any **history of recurrence**. Risk avoided and the quality of available evidence round out the assessment.

## Penalty Mechanisms

After the CMC evaluates the above-mentioned factors and determines an applicable penalty, the Framework provides two options for resolution:

- **General Delayed Penalty**. The manual settlement mechanism, used after the CMC has already made a case-by-case decision that a penalty should be applied. Once decided, the CMC reports a penalty amount (estimated harm plus [applicable penalty fee]([URL] which is locked from the Node Operator's bond. From there, the locked amount is either burned through governance/Easy Track to cover the loss, or released back if the Node Operator compensates directly or the CMC doesn't pursue it further within the period set by the [CMv2 parameters]([URL]
- **Voluntary Compensation Fast Track**. If the NOM team, the CMC, and the Node Operator agree on the incident assessment and compensation amount, the Node Operator may voluntarily compensate the relevant amount to the [PROJECT] Execution Layer Rewards Vault, thereby bypassing the General Delayed Penalty route. However, the CMC and NOM team can still require remediation, post-incident explanation, or monitoring afterwards.

## Review Process

1. NOM identifies incidents through monitoring, validator performance data, relay or builder data, execution layer reward analysis, exit monitoring, key submission checks, public or community reports, Node Operator self-reporting, or other sources. A case may be opened where a material risk is identified, or the circumstances otherwise warrant investigation. At this stage, NOM may also determine whether urgent mitigation or additional information from the Node Operator is required.
2. NOM gathers relevant information, which may include the incident timeline, affected validators and their balances, root cause analysis, infrastructure or configuration details, relay, builder, fee recipient, or reward-flow evidence, and remediation actions already taken or planned by the Node Operator. Failure to provide timely and complete information may be considered an aggravating factor.
3. NOM prepares materials for CMC review, including the incident description, available evidence, Node Operator submissions, affected validators, estimated or actual losses, and any relevant mitigating or aggravating factors. Where precise calculation is not possible, losses may be reasonably estimated using conservative assumptions or other reasonable calculation methods.
4. Reviewing that material alongside the Node Operator’s own submissions and any other relevant information, the CMC may decide that no penalty is warranted, further information or monitoring is required, voluntary compensation is appropriate, a General Delayed Penalty should be applied, the Node Operator’s stake allocation, participation in the Curated set, or type should be reviewed, or the matter should be escalated to the DAO.

## Communication & Disagreement

Each reported penalty is published on the [PROJECT] Research Forum, including the incident description, the basis for the penalty, the category of harm, and the calculation/estimation approach used, subject to any confidentiality, security, or operational limits.

If a Node Operator disagrees with the assessment, the decision, the proposed compensation, or the penalty itself, they can respond on that Research Forum thread with additional evidence, alternative calculations, or mitigating context. The CMC will factor that in where timing allows, but disagreement alone doesn't pause urgent protective action if the CMC judges it necessary to protect the protocol. Separately, the Node Operator should be informed of the determination, its basis, and any expected remediation steps; urgent protective measures can be taken before the investigation is fully complete if needed.

## Framework Maintenance & Future Updates

Approving this Framework also establishes how it will be maintained going forward: the CMC becomes authorised to update operational elements, including incident-assessment thresholds, benchmarks, calculation methodologies, examples, and procedural clarifications, without requiring a separate DAO vote for each change, provided the core principles, penalty mechanisms, Node Operator obligations, and governance structure set out here remain unchanged.

Any change that goes beyond routine maintenance, such as a change that materially affects the scope of penalties, a new penalty mechanism, a material change to Node Operator obligations, or a change to decision-making authority, still requires a full DAO vote. 

All updates made under this maintenance authority, whether routine or otherwise, are published on the Research Forum for visibility.

## Next steps

If approved:

- The Framework becomes the baseline process for assessing and applying penalties to CMv2 Node Operators, effective immediately.
- The CMC will be authorised to maintain and update the Framework’s operational elements, such as incident-assessment thresholds, benchmarks, calculation methodologies, examples, and procedural clarifications, as long as the core principles, penalty mechanisms, Node Operator obligations, and governance structure remain unchanged.

Titel: [PROJECT] ecosystem direction proposal

This proposal asks the [TOKEN] community to decide the fundamental direction of the [PROJECT] ecosystem.
After reading a lot of "suggestions" 
The community must choose whether to:

Option A:  Preserve and Rebuild the [PROJECT] Vision

Continue building the multi-token [PROJECT] ecosystem in which [TOKEN], BONE, LEASH, TREAT and SHI each have separate purposes, beginning with launch of LEASH V2 (it is ready to be launched).

Option B Simplify and Consolidate the Ecosystem

Move away from the existing multi-token structure and develop a plan to consolidate BONE, LEASH, TREAT and other ecosystem functions into one unified token or governance asset alongside [TOKEN].

This proposal selects a direction and if there is any change **needed** in future then it will happen. 

Current Starting Position

Regardless of which option is selected, the community must proceed under the following assumptions and reality:

There is no access to an existing [PROJECT] treasury. In case they did then it should be transferred here [ADDRESS]
There is no guaranteed transfer of funds or holdings from previous ecosystem controllers.
**There is no guaranteed liquidity available for LEASH V2 so whoever wants to add liquidity anyone is free to do so. **
There is no development budget. Any product will be created will have fees (should be explained why and where and how much, everything on chain transparent nothing hidden) as explained before. Any products that will be launched will be owned by me  currently since I do not not see any other proper solution for now and an action should be taken rather than waiting or doing nothing. **Some have reached but I repeat any developer is free to reach me out.**  Any product should be audited before launch. 
The community is effectively rebuilding from zero just how we started in [PROJECT] before.

Any development, liquidity or operational support must therefore come from transparent voluntary participation, new contributions, community builders or future revenue.



Option A Preserve and Rebuild the Original [PROJECT] Vision

Under Option A, the community affirms that the [PROJECT] ecosystem should continue as a collection of assets with distinct purposes.

The proposed structure would remain generally aligned with:

[TOKEN]: The flagship ecosystem token.
BONE: N/A for now
LEASH V2: A rebuilt version of LEASH and same utility as before such as exclusivity for early access and store of value and govern over SHI. 
TREAT:  to be discussed later but a reward token with unlimited supply (producing more when it is needed only controlled by a known multisig and known people in community not random voted by DAO to be part of that multisig and same goes for the management of future treasury but this is early to happen at current stage). 
SHI: A future [PROJECT] ecosystem stablecoin.
new chain: super far in future and very early to even think about now 
Keep in mind a lot of supply of current bone and treat is still controlled under shy and kaal and they keep dumping it until now even recently.  So future migration is highly possible especially TREAT at current stages.

You can imagine all tokens move as a flywheel that benefit each other directly or indirectly such as burns (not fan of but many do think it is a must) or buybacks or whatever through products what will be built or rebuilt **for example** shibaswap (I will not accept launching just a random useless swap, it should be unique or something that can compete with others in the market at least a lesser fee for swapping for example, this is just an example when a project or product will be built to benefit [PROJECT]). The best focus now is to launch products that give utility for [PROJECT] and generate revenue for it. It is a step by step and need a lot of patience.  

First Step: LEASH V2

If Option A is selected, LEASH V2 will be launched first rebuilding project. 
It will be same as original supply 107646.4693.
How it works? 
This contract is a non-rebasing wrapper for the original LEASH token. When you wrap your legacy LEASH, the contract locks your tokens and mints an equivalent amount of the new LEASH based on the legacy token's underlying gons accounting system. It is a separate ERC20 that can be traded anywhere just like any other token such as [TOKEN]. Because the conversion is based on gons rather than the displayed token balance, your proportional ownership is preserved even if the legacy token rebases. 

The wrapped LEASH itself never rebases. Your wallet balance stays fixed, making it much easier to use with wallets, exchanges, and DeFi protocols that expect a standard ERC-20 token.

Example 1: If you wrap 100 legacy LEASH today, those 100 tokens are locked in the wrapper contract and you receive the equivalent amount of new LEASH. Your new LEASH balance remains constant, it will not automatically change because of future rebases from legacy LEASH.

Example 2: If the legacy LEASH supply later doubles due to a rebase or other supply change, your wrapped LEASH balance still stays exactly the same. If you decide to unwrap later, the contract calculates the redemption using the new current legacy supply, ensuring the conversion reflects the latest state of the underlying token.

You are free to move between the two versions whenever you choose. You can wrap legacy LEASH into the new token or unwrap back into the legacy token** at any time** for example because there is a better liquidity in legacy leash you can move there and sell at any moment or when you want to buy, provided the wrapper contract holds your deposited legacy LEASH. No one is forced to migrate, and no one is required to burn their legacy tokens. Wrapping is entirely optional and they can move on or back anytime they want and the contract will do the calculation by itself regardless if you move now or in the future you will not have any advanatge on anyone.

The contract is intentionally simple and has no owner, no admin controls, no transfer taxes, no blacklist, and no hidden mint function. The only way new wrapped LEASH can be created is by depositing legacy LEASH into the wrapper, and the only way wrapped LEASH is removed is when it is redeemed for the underlying legacy LEASH that was previously locked in the contract.
